transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees noted above

Summary (auto): quick parity walk, console walkthrough, talk through pilot mode and security.

[00:00:05] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros?
[00:00:12] Priya (Sentinel): Hey, Priya here, Head of Platform at Sentinel. Marcus and Sophie are with me.
[00:00:18] Marcus (Sentinel): Marcus, ML eng, mostly latency and throughput folks.
[00:00:22] Sophie (Sentinel): Sophie, SRE, will be the operator on the infra side.
[00:00:27] Diego (Redwood SE): Hi, Diego from Redwood engineering, I'll do the deep demo bits.
[00:00:33] Avery: Great, goal for today is to show parity mapping from your current OpenAI/Together stack to Redwood API, show the Console Optimize suggestions for cost/latency, and cover enterprise ops Qs.

[00:01:02] Priya: tl;dr — we need parity for instruction-following and embeddings, and a pilot that proves cost is neutral or better and latency < 300ms p50.
[00:01:12] Avery: Perfect. We'll highlight a few mapping patterns: prompt templates, stop sequences, streaming differences, and model fallbacks.

[00:03:11] Diego: I'm going to share my screen, starting with the Redwood API example. Note the call shape mirrors OpenAI's completion/chat endpoints but with model aliases and explicit rollout tags. Example: you can call /v1/generate?model=redwood-ggml-4x and pass messages or prompt.
[00:03:35] Marcus: any breaking changes in params? like logprobs or temperature behavior?
[00:03:41] Diego: Good question; temperature and top_p behave the same, but tokenization differences mean you might see +/- few tokens — we recommend running the tokenizer parity check we include in the runbook. Also, logprobs supported but field names are slightly different in older SDKs, we map that in the adapter snippet.

[00:06:10] Sophie: how about streaming? we rely on partial tokens in our frontend.
[00:06:18] Diego: Streaming works similarly — Redwood supports chunked streaming over HTTP/2 and SSE. There are a couple of flags for chunk size and flush intervals, we showed the defaults in the Console under model settings. There was a small transcription error earlier where our docs say "k-v cash" sometimes; it's actually KV cache.

[00:08:40] Avery: Now switching to Console: here's the Optimize tab — it surfaces batching suggestions and quantization profiles based on your historical request distribution. For sentinel's use case we flagged high short-context traffic, so we suggested aggressive prefix caching.
[00:09:05] Marcus: aggressive prefix caching — will that impact context window semantics?
[00:09:12] Diego: It preserves semantics — we only cache repeated prefixes across the same session key. For long-form, we recommend sticky routing to a dedicated pool to keep KV cache warm.

[00:11:30] Priya: sticky routing — is this per-tenant or per-route? Our app uses different routes for summarization vs. generation.
[00:11:39] Avery: You can configure routing at per-route level in the Console. We also provide policy rules: latency-first, cost-first, or region-preference.

[00:13:55] Marcus: curious about quantization — Together used a custom q4_0 that saved cost but changed quality. How do you recommend replacing that?
[00:14:03] Diego: Optimize will recommend quantization profiles with an expected BLEU/ROUGE delta and token-cost delta. We encourage running the eval harness we share — it runs your prompt set against model variants and spits out regression/quality metrics. For many customers q4_0-equivalent exists in our catalog, but results vary by workload.

[00:16:40] Sophie: security — KMS and key residency. we have centralized KMS and need envelope encryption.
[00:16:46] Avery: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS in VPC and on-prem. For Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key via our KMS integrations; we log key usage for audit.
[00:17:02] Alan (Sentinel Security): Do you have SOC2 and ISO attestations? We need audit artifacts.
[00:17:08] Avery: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are in the security pack I'll send. Also the Console has audit logs with token-level traces for every inference request.

[00:19:20] Marcus: on throughput — we have bursts up to 800 rps for short windows. Can Redwood handle that with hosted?
[00:19:30] Diego: For bursts we recommend Dedicated pools or combining hosted with burst capacity. Our autoscaler can pre-warm GPUs for scheduled windows. For a pilot we usually allocate a small dedicated pool.

[00:21:05] Priya: downtime and fallbacks — if model variant is unavailable, how do you keep things online?
[00:21:12] Diego: We have automatic fallback policies: you can set a hierarchy of compatible model variants (e.g., redwood-4 -> redwood-4-small -> redwood-3) and traffic will route accordingly. Also multi-region fallback for availability.

[00:23:50] Avery: jumping back to developer experience — porting tips: 1) tokenization parity check, 2) map stop sequences, 3) adapt streaming offsets, 4) use our SDK adapter snippet that acts like OpenAI's API. We'll paste those into the runbook.

[00:26:33] Marcus: anything we should watch for with instruction-following prompts? we saw different behavior across vendors.
[00:26:40] Diego: Yes — model-specific system prompts and temperature interplay. We recommend locking system prompt and running the eval harness to compare outputs on classification accuracy, hallucination rates. Our 'redwood-eval' script will generate side-by-side diffs.

[00:29:00] Sophie: networking — we run in GCP us-west2, need VPC peering and private egress.
[00:29:08] Avery: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and private link connections. For hosted we have customer VPC connectors in major clouds including GCP us-west2.

[00:31:40] Priya: cost — show me a scenario where Redwood is cheaper.
[00:31:46] Diego: Typical win comes from caching and batching — Optimize suggested a 30% cost reduction on you short prompts by reusing prefix tokens and batching 8-12ms windows. Also quantization for non-critical routes. We'll show a sample cost comparison in the runbook spreadsheet.

[00:33:55] Marcus: can we get a sample benchmark run to reproduce? i want p50/p95 numbers on our workload.
[00:34:02] Diego: Absolutely. We'll generate a benchmark script that replays your 48-hour window scaled to your burst patterns. That will produce p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens.

[00:36:10] Alan: legal/procurement — do you require data processing agreements and where's data stored?
[00:36:19] Avery: We have standard DPA and data residency controls. For hosted, customer data is stored in region you select; for Private, all customer data stays in your environment. We'll attach the DPA and example DP flow diagrams.

[00:38:50] Priya: ok so concrete pilot: we want a 1-week pilot with a dedicated small pool and benchmark against our production window. Are there costs?
[00:38:58] Avery: For pilots we typically provide trial credits and ask for a short commitment on a small dedicated pool to guarantee capacity during your bench window. We'll include pricing scenarios in the follow-up.

[00:41:22] Diego: I'm going to demo the runbook converter script now — it takes OpenAI-style calls and produces Redwood-compatible payloads, including mapping stop sequences and streaming boundaries. Note: the converter will flag tokenization mismatches.
[00:41:50] Marcus: nice, can you output a patch for our codebase?
[00:41:55] Diego: Yes, we'll send a small patch and sample unit tests.

[00:44:30] Avery: Questions we didn't cover?
[00:44:36] Sophie: backups and logs retention — for forensic we need 1 year.
[00:44:41] Avery: We support configurable retention windows in Console for audit logs; long-term retention is an add-on.

[00:46:55] Priya: team alignment— who will own the pilot from Redwood?
[00:47:00] Avery: I'll be your AE lead; Diego will run the bench and technical onboarding; Lina will help with Optimize configs.

[00:48:15] Priya: timeline — we want pilot next week if possible.
[00:48:21] Avery: We'll try to stand it up early next week — action items captured.

[00:50:02] Diego: leaving you a link to the Console demo recording and the runbook repo after the call.
[00:50:10] Priya: thanks all, useful.
[00:50:18] Avery: recap: we'll send migration runbook, security pack, pilot script; Sentinel will send prompt set and target windows.
[00:50:35] Marcus: thanks.
[00:50:40] Alan: thanks.
[00:50:45] Diego: thanks everyone, bye.
[00:50:50] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (e.g., "k-v cash" instead of KV cache, "together ai" hyphenation). References shared: runbook repo (link sent in chat), security pack PDF, pilot benchmark spreadsheet.
